newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ Cricket moves to police player buying.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ Cricket moves to police player buying.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Nov 5 - New Zealand Cricket (NZC) is to investigate introducing a transfer system to cover the movement of players around the first-class associations, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
Rugby's controversial transfer legislation is before the Commerce Commission. NZC chief executive Christopher Doig said Friday's board meeting asked for a report into similar regulations for cricket.

"While it has been something that has occurred for years in cricket in New Zealand, this year's situation with Auckland has highlighted some concerns about the practice and the possible need to pay some compensation to associations that invest time and money into player development," Doig said.
Auckland have lost several leading players to other provinces before the coming season's competition.
The board also amended its code of conduct. One of the changes was to increase the maximum fine for a breach of the clothing regulations from $100 to $500.
All associations will be advised of the ban on betting by players and administrators, and reminded of the prospect of penalties being imposed.
Meanwhile, Doig backs a move in South Africa at the weekend to turn on floodlights to extend play in a first-class game where bad light could have had an effect.
A four-day game between Natal and Border at Kingsmead Park in Durban continued under lights, though problems with a sight screen reflecting the lights still resulted in an early finish.
"I can't see any problem with it and I agree with the moves by the chief executive of South Africa's board, Dr Ali Bacher, in this area," Doig said.
"In the longer term, I can see the day when test matches will be played as day-night games.

"You have to play the game at a time when spectators can come along. If it helps people get along to games at a time when they can more easily watch cricket then we have to take the game to the people."
However, Doig does not envisage lights being used at a New Zealand ground this summer.

"It is a different matter in a competition situation where one team might gain an advantage if able to use lights while other games had to be called off. We would have to be a bit careful about it," he said.
At the moment only McLean Park in Napier could be used for lighting, but it is expected Lancaster Park will be fully equipped for day-night cricket before the end of the summer.
